intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that annular epidermolytic ichthyosis-1 (AEI1) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the keratin-10 gene (KRT10; 148080) on chromosome 17q21.2.

checks.claim: Annular epidermolytic ichthyosis-1 (AEI1) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the keratin-10 gene (KRT10).
checks.evidence_quote: Molecular analysis revealed a novel tandem CG to GA 2-bp mutation in the same allele of keratin 10 in affected individuals
checks.explanation: KRT10 mutation in AEI is reported; heterozygosity is implied by dominant inheritance but not stated explicitly in the abstract.

checks.claim: The KRT10 gene is located on chromosome 17q21.2.
checks.evidence_quote: Molecular analysis revealed a novel tandem CG to GA 2-bp mutation in the same allele of keratin 10
checks.explanation: Chromosomal location is standard nomenclature restating the gene.

paragraphs.text: Annular epidermolytic ichthyosis is a form of epidermolytic (acanthokeratolytic) ichthyosis. Bullous ichthyosis begins in early childhood and is followed by hyperkeratotic, lichenified plaques in flexural and extensor areas. A characteristic feature is intermittent bouts of annular and polycyclic, erythematous, scaly or hyperkeratotic plaques on the trunk and proximal extremities, which resolve. Histology shows epidermolytic hyperkeratosis (Sahn et al., 1992; Suga et al., 1998).

checks.evidence_quote: This kindred may represent a new phenotype of epidermolytic (acanthokeratolytic) ichthyosis.
checks.explanation: The paper puts this tentatively ('may represent'); the draft states it as fact.

paragraphs.text: Sahn et al. (1992) reported a 30-year-old white woman who developed bullous and ichthyosiform skin lesions at the age of 8 months. The blistering stopped at puberty, but the hyperkeratotic plaques persisted. At age 27 years, she developed numerous annular and polycyclic, erythematous, hyperkeratotic plaques on the trunk and extremities. These plaques were pruritic, enlarged slowly, and then resolved. Histopathology showed epidermolytic hyperkeratosis. On electron microscopy, the annular plaques showed interrupted perinuclear tonofilament rings, consistent with either bullous ichthyotic erythroderma of Brocq or ichthyosis bullosa of Siemens. Two of her 5 children were affected with a bullous type of ichthyosis. The authors suggested that this kindred may represent a new phenotype of epidermolytic ichthyosis.

paragraphs.text: Joh et al. (1997) reported a second occurrence of annular epidermolytic ichthyosis, in a family with 2 affected generations. The proband had bullous ichthyosis with bouts of disease activity, during which numerous annular and polycyclic, erythematous, hyperkeratotic plaques developed on the trunk and proximal extremities. Histology showed epidermolytic hyperkeratosis, with abnormal keratin filament networks and clumping of perinuclear tonofilaments.

Affected individuals had bullous ichthyosis in early childhood, followed by hyperkeratotic, lichenified plaques in flexural areas and on extensor surfaces. They had characteristic intermittent bouts of annular and polycyclic, erythematous, scaly plaques on the trunk and proximal extremities.

paragraphs.text: Mikilita et al. (2020) reported an 8-year-old Brazilian girl, born to nonconsanguineous parents, who had a diffuse dermatosis that began in the first months of life. On examination, she had erythematous, scaly, hyperkeratotic plaques with prominent borders. These affected the mesogastrium, cubital and popliteal fossae, and inguinal and cervical regions. The plaques were migratory and polycyclic. She also had palmoplantar hyperkeratosis and yellowish hyperkeratotic plaques on the scalp and nasal introitus. She had no hair, nail, or mucosal abnormalities. A skin biopsy from the extensor forearm showed acanthosis, papillomatosis, and hyperkeratosis, with marked epidermolysis in the granular layer. In a review of literature published in English, Portuguese, and Spanish since the first description by Sahn et al. (1992), Mikilita et al. (2020) found 19 cases of annular epidermolytic ichthyosis in 10 publications.

paragraphs.text: Mikilita et al. (2020) noted that the main differential diagnosis of annular epidermolytic ichthyosis is erythrokeratodermia variabilis et progressiva (EKVP). EKVP is distinguished by onset during childhood, absence of epidermal fragility, and histology without epidermolysis. Their patient was first diagnosed with EKVP, and the diagnosis was revised after a biopsy showed epidermolytic hyperkeratosis.
